name: American blackface-style clean (6L6 pair)
notes: Mid-60s American clean style: sparkling highs, deep scooped mids, lots of headroom. Path: V1a -> tone stack driven straight from the plate (no cathode follower) -> volume -> V2a -> phase inverter (12AT7) -> 2x 6L6GC with strong feedback and no presence control. FROM SCHEMATICS (fairly sure): 12AX7 stages with 100k plate resistors and 1.5k/25 uF cathodes; tone stack 250p treble cap, 0.1u bass cap, 0.047u mid cap, 250k treble and bass pots, 100k slope resistor, a fixed 6.8k resistor instead of a mid pot (so 'mid' is set to 10), driven from the plate (about 38k source); 12AT7 long-tailed pair phase inverter; 6L6GC pair. UNSURE / APPROXIMATED: the real amp has a reverb mixing stage between V2 and the phase inverter; it is left out and only its loss is kept (-18 dB, a guess: without it the phase inverter was overdriven and the preset distorted 26% when played hard); phase inverter as one triode that gets half the input (each triode of the real long-tailed pair sees half the signal, so it has twice the headroom of a single stage); feedback amount (set for about 10 dB); output into 4.2k. POWER SUPPLY: GZ34 tube rectifier plus the winding, as 170 ohm into 70 uF (supply_ohms, supply_uf on the power block), so the sag comes from the current the power tubes really draw. These two values are GUESSES from typical parts, not from this amp's schematic. (It replaced a sag block.) COUPLING: every tube stage STARTS with its coupling capacitor into its grid resistor (coupling_nf, grid_ohms; default 22 nF into 1 Mohm = 7.2 Hz; power tubes 22 nF into 220k = 33 Hz), a 1st-order high-pass, and its bias shift recovers in C x R through that same capacitor (the guessed release times are gone). The small capacitors of tight stages (0.6-2 nF, from the old 80-250 Hz high-passes) recover in 1-2 ms: that is why tight amps use them. The output transformer's low end stays a post highpass1. PREAMP SUPPLY: every gain stage (v1a, v2a, pi) hangs on the same supply through decoupling filters (preamp_targets), so it sags too, about 100 ms behind (preamp_filter_ms: a GUESS; real amps have 10k-ish resistors and 10-50 uF capacitors per node). OUTPUT TRANSFORMER: the core of a 40 W amp's transformer, saturating on full-power notes below about 40 Hz (transformer_sat_hz: a GUESS from the amp's size, not measured): loud low notes lose bass and get odd harmonics.
